# TriageX Simulation Assumptions

> **Synthetic hospital operations simulation — not real-time hospital data.**
> Hospital names and approximate coordinates are used only for map context. Every
> capacity, staffing, demand, and outcome figure is synthetic and describes no real
> hospital. No hospital supplied data to, approved, or partnered with this project.

This document lists every modeling assumption in the Phase 2 engine
(`backend/app/simulation/`), so results can be read for what they are: the output of a
simple, transparent model, not a validated prediction.

## Time

- One tick is 15 simulated minutes. The horizon is 96 ticks (24 hours).
- Each scenario has a 24-tick (6-hour) demo window covering its surge.
- Wait and handoff times therefore have 15-minute resolution.
- Before tick 0, 32 ticks (8 hours) of ordinary demand are simulated so hospitals start
  partly occupied. This warm-up is identical in both tracks and excluded from metrics.

## Hospitals (all values synthetic)

| Hospital | Treatment spaces | Base staff | Staffed capacity | Base arrivals/hour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grady Memorial | 56 | 13 | 45 | 9.5 |
| Emory University Hospital | 40 | 9 | 31 | 6.5 |
| Emory University Hospital Midtown | 44 | 10 | 35 | 7.5 |
| Piedmont Atlanta | 42 | 10 | 35 | 7.0 |
| Wellstar Kennestone | 52 | 12 | 42 | 9.0 |

- **Staffed capacity** = `min(treatment spaces, floor(staff × 3.5))`. Extra staff never
  create physical space. For example, Grady can use at most 3 extra staff (45 → 56).
- Staff are "nurse-equivalents" with a constant roster; shift changes are not modeled.
- Separate surge spaces (hallway beds) from the Phase 0 plan are not modeled.

## Demand

- Arrivals per hospital per tick are Poisson with rate
  `base × diurnal(clock hour) × scenario multiplier`.
- The diurnal profile is synthetic (low overnight, peak around midday).
- 20–26% of ordinary arrivals come by ambulance.
- Acuity is 1 (most urgent) to 3. Walk-ins: 6% / 44% / 50%. Ambulance: 28% / 52% / 20%.
- Treatment time is lognormal by acuity (means of 300, 200 and 100 minutes; σ = 0.45),
  scaled by the scenario's service multiplier.
- Every patient is sampled once, before either track runs. Both tracks receive the same
  immutable patient tuple.

## Queue and service

- Each hospital has one queue, ordered by acuity, then ED arrival tick, then a stable
  sequence number.
- A patient occupies one staffed space for their whole treatment time.
- If staffing drops below current occupancy, nobody is removed; new placements simply
  wait.
- **Saturation** = `(patients in treatment + patients waiting) / treatment spaces`.
  Status is normal below 85%, pressure from 85% to just under 100%, and breach at 100%
  or more.

## Ambulance handoff and diversion (both tracks)

- An ambulance crew is held from ED arrival until its patient is placed. That interval
  is the handoff wait.
- A hospital goes on diversion after 2 consecutive ticks at saturation of 100% or more
  with at least one ambulance waiting. It comes off diversion below 90%.
- While a hospital is diverting, non-critical ambulances (acuity 2–3) go to the nearest
  hospital that is not diverting. Acuity-1 ambulances are never diverted. If every
  hospital is diverting, ambulances continue to their intended hospital.
- Reroute travel = 5 minutes plus straight-line distance × 1.3 at 45 km/h, rounded up to
  whole ticks (at least one).
- **Ambulance-hours lost** = handoff waiting hours plus extra reroute travel hours.

## Forecast

- The forecast projects saturation two hours ahead with a fluid model, using only an
  `ObservedState`: current occupancy, queue, and staffed capacity; arrivals in the
  trailing hour; the ordinary diurnal shape; and a fixed 170-minute length-of-stay
  prior.
- It does not see the scenario definition or any future arrival. A test replaces all
  future arrivals and checks that earlier forecasts do not change.
- The forecast is simple and noisy. Across 5 seeds × 4 scenarios, its error at 2 hours is
  roughly unbiased (−6 to +2 percentage points) with a mean absolute error of 11–14
  points. During a sudden burst it overshoots, because it cannot know the burst will end.
- **Proposal rule:** when the forecast reaches 90% or more, the engine raises a staffing
  proposal (if extra staff can still add capacity) and a level-loading proposal. It
  re-arms only after the forecast drops below 80%.
- False alarms happen. For example, Grady can trip the threshold during ordinary midday
  peaks.

## TriageX interventions (Track B only, human-approved inputs)

- **Staffing**
  - Each confirmation adds one staff member.
  - Effect starts 45 simulated minutes (3 ticks) after the operator approves the
    request, and lasts 4 hours (16 ticks).
  - A confirmation's simulated effect never depends on when the real reply arrives.
  - Capacity is still capped by treatment spaces.
- **Level-loading**
  - Starts 15 minutes after approval and lasts 4 hours.
  - Up to 2 acuity-3 ambulances per tick are sent to the nearest hospital that is not
    diverting, whose forecast at the previous tick was below 80%, and that has accepted
    fewer than 2 redirects that tick.
  - If the source hospital is already diverting, level-loading only chooses the receiver
    using forecasts, and the patient still counts as diverted.
  - When it redirects patients from a hospital that is not diverting, these count as
    transfers.
- With no interventions, Track B is identical to Track A. Tests check this.

## Metrics

- Patient metrics cover patients whose ED arrival falls inside the measured range.
- Patients still waiting at the end of the horizon contribute a censored wait (horizon
  end minus arrival), so long queues are never dropped.
- Percentiles use the nearest-rank method.
- Percent changes are computed from the two tracks' values. None are hardcoded.

## Scenarios

| Scenario | Tick 0 | Demo window | Main assumption |
|---|---|---|---|
| I-85 Multi-Vehicle Pileup | 12:00 | 15:00–21:00 | 67 extra, mostly high-acuity ambulance patients from 16:00, front-loaded over 2 hours; 42 expected at Grady |
| Big Game Downtown | 12:00 | 21:00–03:00 | Demand up to 2.5× at Grady and 2.2× at Midtown from 22:00, plus 44 crowd-injury arrivals |
| Summer Heat Wave | 08:00 | 13:00–19:00 | Metro-wide demand up to 1.4× from 13:00 to 20:00, 10% longer treatment times, more ambulances |
| Respiratory Illness Wave | 06:00 | 16:00–22:00 | 1.15× all day (about 1.32× in the evening), 10% longer treatment times |

## Robustness (20 seeds each)

The demo intervention is the first surge-time staffing proposal: the recommended staff,
plus level-loading, approved 15 minutes after the proposal. These figures are demo-window
changes, Track B minus Track A.

| Scenario | Mean wait change (median, range) | Ambulance-hours change (median, range) | Seeds where TriageX was worse |
|---|---|---|---|
| I-85 Pileup | −11.3 min (−16.6 to −3.4) | −17.6 h (−35.8 to −3.2) | none on wait or ambulance-hours; 1 on diversions |
| Big Game | −5.8 min (−18.0 to −0.4) | −3.6 h (−19.5 to +0.2) | 1 on ambulance-hours |
| Heat Wave | −6.8 min (−14.1 to +0.1) | −2.9 h (−12.2 to +2.0) | 1 on wait; 5 on ambulance-hours; 2 on diversions |
| Respiratory Wave | 0.0 min (−11.5 to +0.2) | 0.0 h (−2.2 to 0.0) | 2 on wait |

Respiratory Wave shows little effect. Its first proposal often comes from a hospital
that is not the binding constraint, and demand stays high for longer than the 4-hour
shift. That is a model result, not a bug.

## Known limitations

- Not clinically validated. There is no boarding, inpatient bed flow, lab or imaging
  delay, or left-without-being-seen behavior.
- Staffing is a single pooled number per hospital.
- Level-loading assumes EMS complies immediately.
- Determinism is exact on a given platform and Python version. Floating-point library
  differences across platforms could change results.

content.text:
The Phase 2 engine is built, committed as `f0e9f13`, and pushed, and Entire captured this session. The I-85 demo works as designed: both tracks are identical until the confirmed staff start their shift, then the TriageX track separates.

## 1. Files

**Simulation code, new** (in `backend/app/simulation/`):
- [models.py](backend/app/simulation/models.py): data types
- [hospitals.py](backend/app/simulation/hospitals.py): the five-hospital network and travel times
- [scenarios.py](backend/app/simulation/scenarios.py): the four scenarios
- [arrivals.py](backend/app/simulation/arrivals.py): all random sampling
- [forecast.py](backend/app/simulation/forecast.py): the two-hour projection
- [interventions.py](backend/app/simulation/interventions.py): staffing and level-loading
- [engine.py](backend/app/simulation/engine.py): the 15-minute tick loop
- [metrics.py](backend/app/simulation/metrics.py): computed results
- [comparison.py](backend/app/simulation/comparison.py): runs both tracks and computes deltas
- [cli.py](backend/app/simulation/cli.py): command-line report

**Tests, new** (in `backend/tests/`): [sim_helpers.py](backend/tests/sim_helpers.py) plus six `test_sim_*.py` files.

**Docs:** [docs/assumptions.md](docs/assumptions.md) is new. [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md) and [README.md](README.md) are updated.

**Changes to the approved plan:**
- Three extra modules (`arrivals`, `comparison`, `cli`), all inside `simulation/`.
- Separate surge spaces (hallway beds) are not modeled.
- An 8-hour warm-up runs before tick 0 so hospitals don't start empty. It is identical in both tracks and excluded from metrics.
- Frontend code is untouched.

## 2. How the simulation works

- **Patients:** every arrival is sampled once, before either track runs. Both tracks get the same unchangeable list, so all randomness happens up front.
- **Engine:** each 15-minute tick applies staffing, discharges patients, lands rerouted ambulances, routes new arrivals, places waiting patients in priority order, then records state, diversion, the forecast and any proposals.
- **Determinism:** the engine is a pure function of scenario, seed and interventions. Seeds are derived with SHA-256, so they don't depend on Python's hash randomization.
- **Both tracks have reactive diversion.** TriageX only adds interventions a human approved.
- **Staffing:** takes effect 45 minutes after approval, lasts 4 hours, and is capped by physical treatment spaces.
- **Level-loading:** sends least-urgent ambulances to hospitals forecast below 80%. If the source hospital is already diverting, it only picks a better receiver and the patient still counts as diverted, so the diversion metric isn't flattered.
- **Forecast:** sees only an `ObservedState` snapshot of current occupancy, queue, staffing and the last hour's arrivals. It never sees the scenario definition or future arrivals.

## 3. I-85 example (seed 42, demo window 15:00–21:00)

Timeline: the pileup starts at 16:00. TriageX proposes 3 staff for Grady at 16:15, and the operator approves at 16:30. Grady's baseline goes on diversion at 16:45, when level-loading also starts. The 3 staff start at 17:15, which is also when the two tracks first differ. Grady's capacity goes from 45 to 56, and all 3 confirmations are usable.

| Metric (window) | Baseline | TriageX | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mean wait | 14.24 min | 6.93 min | −51.3% |
| 90th-percentile wait | 75 min | 30 min | −60.0% |
| Peak saturation | 110.71% | 110.71% | 0.0% (peak is at 16:45, before any effect) |
| Hospital-ticks in breach | 17 | 7 | −58.8% |
| Ambulance handoff hours | 25.50 | 14.25 | −44.1% |
| Ambulance-hours lost (handoff + reroute travel) | 28.00 | 16.75 | −40.2% |
| Diversion onsets / ambulances diverted | 2 / 10 | 1 / 7 | improved |

**Robustness over 20 seeds** (demo-window change, TriageX minus baseline):

| Scenario | Mean wait change | Ambulance-hours change | Seeds where TriageX was worse |
|---|---|---|---|
| I-85 | −11.3 min median | −17.6 h median | none on wait or ambulance-hours; 1 on diversions |
| Big Game | −5.8 min median | −3.6 h median | 1 on ambulance-hours |
| Heat Wave | −6.8 min median | −2.9 h median | 1 on wait, 5 on ambulance-hours, 2 on diversions |
| Respiratory Wave | 0.0 min median | 0.0 h median | 2 on wait |

Respiratory Wave shows almost no benefit. I left that as the model's honest result rather than tuning it.

## 4. Test results

- **Backend:** 86 passed, 82 of them new. Ruff lint and format checks are clean.
- **Frontend:** 2 passed, unchanged.

The new tests cover:
- **Determinism:** replay for all scenarios, plus a subprocess check under two different hash seeds.
- **Track equality:** Track B equals baseline with no interventions.
- **Timing:** nothing changes before the 45-minute lead time, and the queue is not reduced at confirmation.
- **Recalculation:** extra confirmations change only what comes after they take effect.
- **Capacity:** 10 confirmations still cap Grady at 56 (3 usable, 7 blocked), and staffing only changes the authorized hospital.
- **Handoff arithmetic:** hand-built networks with exact expected answers.
- **Forecast isolation:** replacing all future arrivals leaves earlier forecasts unchanged.
- **Ledger check:** occupancy and queues in every tick match the patient records, across all scenarios and both tracks.
- **Level-loading:** its receiver and per-tick limits are respected.

## 5. Performance

Medians over 20 runs:

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| Patient generation (about 1,200 patients) | 8 ms |
| One track | 10–11 ms |
| Full comparison (both tracks plus metrics) | 31–35 ms |

Re-running Track B after each confirmation is effectively instant.

## 6. Known limitations

- The forecast's two-hour error averages 11–14 percentage points of saturation. It overshoots during sudden bursts and sometimes raises false alarms; for example, Grady can trip the threshold at an ordinary midday peak.
- Not clinically validated: no inpatient boarding, no lab delays, no patients leaving without being seen, and staffing is one pooled number per hospital.
- Waits have 15-minute resolution.
- Results are exactly reproducible on one platform and Python version, but floating-point differences across platforms could change them.
- The tuning changes during this phase are documented as assumptions.

## 7. Is the live demo supported?

At the engine level, yes. Every requirement is in place:
- a shared timeline for both tracks;
- approval, 45-minute lead, shift-active, shift-end and divergence markers;
- the 6-hour window;
- re-running Track B with an updated confirmation count.

Delivering it to the dashboard needs the Phase 3 API.

## 8. Git and Entire

- **Commit:** `f0e9f139e2ac4403c4861c2fde2d2c6036c043fb`, pushed. Local `main` matches `origin/main`.
- **Entire:** checkpoint `01M7C4WRH5Z2J674Z7DPQ0J0EH` is on GitHub, and `entire checkpoint list --outgoing` reports nothing queued. Its transcript includes the Phase 2 conversation.
- **Entire metadata gap:** the checkpoint's `files_touched` list names only `README.md` and `docs/plan.md`, not the 18 new files. It appears to record edited files but not newly created ones.

Phase 2 complete. Awaiting approval to begin Phase 3.

## Hackathon Demo and Pitch Priority — Critical

TriageX is being built for a live hackathon presentation. Our primary goal is to demonstrate a compelling, visually clear, end-to-end hospital surge coordination system.

Every backend decision should support the following experience:

**Surge predicted → Human approves outreach → Staff confirms → Intervention becomes active → Two simulated futures visibly diverge → Measurable impact appears.**

Design the API responses so the frontend can deliver this entire experience on a single screen without unnecessary navigation or waiting.

Specifically:

1. **Cinematic demo progression:** Return the data needed for a smooth timeline replay, including hospital status transitions, forecast alerts, approval events, confirmation events, staffing lead-time bands, shift-start markers, and comparison curves.

2. **Strong visual storytelling:** Make it straightforward for the frontend to animate the transition from identical baseline and intervention curves to visibly different outcomes after the intervention becomes active.

3. **Hero metrics:** Prioritize ambulance handoff hours, patient waiting time, and hospital recovery. Return computed absolute differences and percentage changes so the frontend doesn't need to calculate them.

4. **Instant interaction:** Aim for the confirmed staffing response to trigger an updated comparison in under 200 ms locally. Measure the actual latency rather than assuming it.

5. **Six-hour demo window:** Provide a ready-to-render six-hour timeline for the I-85 scenario, while preserving the underlying 24-hour simulation.

6. **Single-screen presentation:** Design response schemas for a dashboard containing an Atlanta hospital map, synchronized comparison charts, a live coordination feed, and one prominent impact metric.

7. **Reliable demo reset:** Support returning the application to the same initial scenario and timeline so we can rehearse the presentation repeatedly.

8. **Presentation-friendly event labels:** Provide concise event titles such as "Surge Predicted," "Outreach Approved," "Staff Confirmed," and "Shift Active."

9. **Authentic results:** All metrics must come from the simulation. Never fabricate improvements, modify historical results, or make the intervention appear effective before its simulated activation time.

10. **Keep technical limitations out of the main demo narrative:** Present the strongest verified capabilities and computed results prominently. Keep engineering diagnostics available for development and judge Q&A, rather than cluttering the presentation screen.

The desired result is not simply a functioning API. It is an API specifically designed to power a memorable, polished, 90-second live demonstration.

Do not implement the frontend during Phase 3. Just make sure the API supports this experience.

"""Response schemas for the single-screen TriageX dashboard.

One `DashboardState` carries everything the command center renders: map, synchronized
comparison curves, coordination feed, proposal cards, and the hero impact metric. All
numbers are computed by the simulation; the frontend never derives deltas itself.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

TrackName = Literal["baseline", "triagex"]
StatusName = Literal["normal", "pressure", "breach"]
Origin = Literal["simulation", "operator", "simulated_reply", "webhook"]
Severity = Literal["info", "warning", "critical", "success"]
CurvePhase = Literal["before_intervention", "staff_en_route", "shift_active", "after_shift"]


class ScenarioSummary(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str
    description: str
    focus_hospital_id: str
    surge_onset_tick: int


class RunInfo(BaseModel):
    run_id: str
    version: int = Field(description="Increments every time Track B is recalculated")
    scenario: ScenarioSummary
    seed: int
    created_at: datetime
    notice: str


class TimeWindow(BaseModel):
    start_tick: int
    end_tick: int  # exclusive
    start_clock: str
    end_clock: str


class Timeline(BaseModel):
    tick_minutes: int
    horizon_ticks: int
    clocks: list[str] = Field(description="Clock label for every tick in the 24-hour horizon")
    demo_window: TimeWindow
    suggested_ms_per_tick: int


class HospitalInfo(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str
    short_name: str
    lat: float
    lon: float
    treatment_spaces: int
    base_staff: int


class HospitalPoint(BaseModel):
    tick: int
    status: StatusName
    saturation_pct: float
    occupied: int
    queue_length: int
    ambulances_waiting: int
    staff_on_duty: int
    staffed_capacity: int
    mean_wait_minutes: float
    forecast_saturation_pct: float
    diverting: bool


class HospitalSeries(BaseModel):
    hospital_id: str
    baseline: list[HospitalPoint]
    triagex: list[HospitalPoint]


class CurvePoint(BaseModel):
    """One tick of the six-hour demo window, both futures side by side."""

    tick: int
    clock: str
    phase: CurvePhase
    diverged: bool
    baseline_focus_saturation_pct: float
    triagex_focus_saturation_pct: float
    baseline_patients_waiting: int
    triagex_patients_waiting: int
    baseline_ambulances_waiting: int
    triagex_ambulances_waiting: int
    baseline_ambulance_hours_cumulative: float
    triagex_ambulance_hours_cumulative: float
    ambulance_hours_saved_so_far: float


class Curves(BaseModel):
    focus_hospital_id: str
    window: TimeWindow
    points: list[CurvePoint]


class Band(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["demo_window", "staff_lead_time", "shift_active", "level_loading_active"]
    start_tick: int
    end_tick: int
    label: str

class Marker(BaseModel):
    tick: int
    clock: str
    kind: str
    label: str
    hospital_id: str | None = None


class StatusTransition(BaseModel):
    tick: int
    clock: str
    track: TrackName
    hospital_id: str
    from_status: StatusName
    to_status: StatusName


class Flow(BaseModel):
    """Ambulances rerouted between hospitals in one tick (for map animation)."""

    tick: int
    track: TrackName
    from_hospital_id: str
    to_hospital_id: str
    kind: Literal["diversion", "level_loading"]
    count: int
    travel_ticks: int


class FeedEvent(BaseModel):
    id: str
    tick: int
    clock: str
    title: str
    detail: str
    kind: str
    track: Literal["both", "baseline", "triagex"]
    origin: Origin
    severity: Severity
    hospital_id: str | None = None
    wall_time: datetime | None = None


class ProposalCard(BaseModel):
    id: str
    kind: Literal["staffing", "level_loading"]
    hospital_id: str
    tick: int
    clock: str
    title: str
    rationale: str
    forecast_saturation_pct: float
    current_saturation_pct: float
    recommended_staff: int | None
    status: Literal["available", "approved"]
    recommended: bool


class Confirmation(BaseModel):
    staff_id: str
    display_name: str
    source: Literal["simulated", "webhook"]
    received_at: datetime


class StaffingRequestView(BaseModel):
    request_id: str
    proposal_id: str
    hospital_id: str
    requested_staff: int
    confirmed_staff: int
    usable_staff: int
    status: Literal["awaiting_replies", "partially_confirmed", "fully_confirmed", "expired"]
    approved_tick: int
    effective_tick: int
    end_tick: int
    approved_at: datetime
    expires_at: datetime
    confirmations: list[Confirmation]


class HeroMetric(BaseModel):
    key: str
    label: str
    unit: str
    baseline: float
    triagex: float
    delta: float
    pct_change: float | None
    lower_is_better: bool
    improved: bool | None
    headline: str


class RecoveryView(BaseModel):
    hospital_id: str
    baseline_recovered_tick: int | None
    triagex_recovered_tick: int | None
    baseline_recovered_clock: str | None
    triagex_recovered_clock: str | None
    minutes_sooner: int | None
    baseline_breach_hours: float
    triagex_breach_hours: float
    headline: str


class Impact(BaseModel):
    state: Literal["awaiting_intervention", "staff_en_route", "intervention_active"]

class Divergence(BaseModel):

class Meta(BaseModel):

class DashboardState(BaseModel):

class ForecastAccuracy(BaseModel):

class Diagnostics(BaseModel):

"""In-memory demo runs: scenario state, operator approvals, and staff confirmations.

The baseline track and the patient stream are computed once per run and never change.
Each staff confirmation re-simulates Track B only, with the same patients, then the
comparison is rebuilt. History is never rewritten: a confirmation's simulated effect
starts at the approved request time plus the staffing lead time, regardless of when the
reply arrives in real time.

Phase 4 moves persistence to Tiger Data; this store is process-local.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading
import time
import uuid
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

from app.simulation.arrivals import generate_patients
from app.simulation.comparison import Comparison, build_comparison
from app.simulation.engine import simulate
from app.simulation.hospitals import DEFAULT_NETWORK, Network
from app.simulation.interventions import (
    Intervention,
    LevelLoadingIntervention,
    StaffingIntervention,
)
from app.simulation.metrics import Metrics, summarize
from app.simulation.models import Proposal, Track, TrackResult
from app.simulation.scenarios import Scenario, get_scenario

log = logging.getLogger("triagex.demo")

DEFAULT_SCENARIO_ID = "i85_pileup"
DEFAULT_SEED = 42
DEFAULT_REQUEST_TTL = timedelta(minutes=10)

# Fictional demo staff. Phase 6 maps opted-in teammates' phones onto these identities.
DEMO_STAFF: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
    ("rn-avery", "Avery (fictional RN)"),
    ("rn-jordan", "Jordan (fictional RN)"),
    ("rn-morgan", "Morgan (fictional RN)"),
    ("rn-riley", "Riley (fictional RN)"),
    ("rn-casey", "Casey (fictional RN)"),
    ("rn-quinn", "Quinn (fictional RN)"),
)
STAFF_NAMES = dict(DEMO_STAFF)


class NotFoundError(LookupError):
    pass


class ConflictError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass(slots=True)
class ConfirmationRecord:
    staff_id: str
    display_name: str
    source: str  # "simulated" now; "webhook" once Chert is integrated
    received_at: datetime
    recompute_ms: float


@dataclass(slots=True)
class StaffingRequest:
    request_id: str
    proposal_id: str
    hospital_id: str
    requested_staff: int
    approved_tick: int
    approved_at: datetime
    expires_at: datetime
    operator: str
    confirmations: list[ConfirmationRecord] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def confirmed_staff(self) -> int:
        return len(self.confirmations)

    def intervention(self) -> StaffingIntervention:
        return StaffingIntervention(
            id=self.request_id,
            hospital_id=self.hospital_id,
            approved_tick=self.approved_tick,
            confirmed_staff=self.confirmed_staff,
        )


@dataclass(slots=True)
class OperatorAction:
    kind: str  # "outreach_approved" | "level_loading_approved"
    tick: int
    wall_time: datetime
    hospital_id: str
    proposal_id: str
    operator: str


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Run:
    run_id: str
    scenario: Scenario
    seed: int
    created_at: datetime
    network: Network
    patients: tuple
    baseline: TrackResult
    baseline_metrics: tuple[Metrics, Metrics]
    comparison: Comparison
    version: int = 1
    staffing_requests: dict[str, StaffingRequest] = field(default_factory=dict)
    level_loading: dict[str, LevelLoadingIntervention] = field(default_factory=dict)
    approved_proposals: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    actions: list[OperatorAction] = field(default_factory=list)
    recompute_history_ms: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)
    last_recompute_ms: float | None = None

    def interventions(self) -> tuple[Intervention, ...]:
        staffing = [r.intervention() for r in self.staffing_requests.values()]
        return (*staffing, *self.level_loading.values())

    def find_proposal(self, proposal_id: str) -> Proposal:
        for source in (self.comparison.triagex.proposals, self.baseline.proposals):
            for p in source:
                if p.id == proposal_id:
                    return p
        raise NotFoundError(f"Proposal '{proposal_id}' not found")

    def recommended_proposal(self) -> Proposal | None:
        """The demo's headline proposal: first surge-time staffing proposal at the focus
        hospital (falling back to the first surge-time staffing proposal anywhere)."""
        onset = self.scenario.surge_onset_tick
        staffing = [p for p in self.baseline.proposals if p.kind == "staffing" and p.tick >= onset]
        focus = [p for p in staffing if p.hospital_id == self.scenario.focus_hospital_id]
        return (focus or staffing or [None])[0]

    def recompute(self) -> float:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        triagex = simulate(
            self.network, self.scenario, self.patients, self.interventions(), Track.TRIAGEX
        )
        self.comparison = build_comparison(
            self.scenario,
            self.seed,
            self.patients,
            self.baseline,
            triagex,
            self.network,
            baseline_metrics=self.baseline_metrics,
        )
        elapsed = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
        self.last_recompute_ms = elapsed
        self.recompute_history_ms.append(elapsed)
        return elapsed


class DemoService:
    def __init__(
        self,
        network: Network = DEFAULT_NETWORK,
        request_ttl: timedelta = DEFAULT_REQUEST_TTL,
        clock: Callable[[], datetime] = lambda: datetime.now(UTC),
    ):
        self.network = network
        self.request_ttl = request_ttl
        self.clock = clock
        self._lock = threading.RLock()
        self._runs: dict[str, Run] = {}
        self._active_run_id: str | None = None

    # --- runs -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def create_run(self, scenario_id: str = DEFAULT_SCENARIO_ID, seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED) -> Run:
        scenario = get_scenario(scenario_id)
        started = time.perf_counter()
        patients = generate_patients(self.network, scenario, seed)
        baseline = simulate(self.network, scenario, patients, (), Track.BASELINE)
        baseline_metrics = (summarize(baseline), summarize(baseline, tick_range=scenario.demo_window))
        triagex = simulate(self.network, scenario, patients, (), Track.TRIAGEX)
        comparison = build_comparison(
            scenario, seed, patients, baseline, triagex, self.network, baseline_metrics
        )
        run = Run(
            run_id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:12],
            scenario=scenario,
            seed=seed,
            created_at=self.clock(),
            network=self.network,
            patients=patients,
            baseline=baseline,
            baseline_metrics=baseline_metrics,
            comparison=comparison,
        )
        run.last_recompute_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
        with self._lock:
            self._runs[run.run_id] = run
            self._active_run_id = run.run_id
        log.info("run created", extra={"run_id": run.run_id, "scenario": scenario_id, "seed": seed})
        return run

    def reset(self, scenario_id: str = DEFAULT_SCENARIO_ID, seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED) -> Run:
        """Discard every run and start the demo again from the same initial state."""
        with self._lock:
            self._runs.clear()
            self._active_run_id = None
            return self.create_run(scenario_id, seed)

    def get_run(self, run_id: str) -> Run:
        with self._lock:
            try:
                return self._runs[run_id]
            except KeyError:
                raise NotFoundError(f"Run '{run_id}' not found") from None

    def active_run(self) -> Run:
        with self._lock:
            if self._active_run_id is None:
                return self.create_run()
            return self._runs[self._active_run_id]

    # --- operator actions -----------------------------------------------------------
    def approve_proposal(
        self, run_id: str, proposal_id: str, at_tick: int | None = None, operator: str = "operator"
    ) -> tuple[Run, str]:
        """Approve a proposal. Returns the run and the created request/intervention id."""
        with self._lock:
            run = self.get_run(run_id)
            proposal = run.find_proposal(proposal_id)
            if proposal_id in run.approved_proposals:
                raise ConflictError(f"Proposal '{proposal_id}' is already approved")
            tick = proposal.tick if at_tick is None else at_tick
            if not (proposal.tick <= tick < run.scenario.horizon_ticks):
                raise ConflictError(
                    f"Approval tick {tick} must be between the proposal tick {proposal.tick} "
                    f"and the end of the horizon"
                )
            now = self.clock()
            if proposal.kind == "staffing":
                request_id = f"req-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
                run.staffing_requests[request_id] = StaffingRequest(
                    request_id=request_id,
                    proposal_id=proposal.id,
                    hospital_id=proposal.hospital_id,
                    requested_staff=proposal.recommended_staff or 1,
                    approved_tick=tick,
                    approved_at=now,
                    expires_at=now + self.request_ttl,
                    operator=operator,
                )
                created = request_id
                kind = "outreach_approved"
            else:
                created = f"ll-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
                run.level_loading[created] = LevelLoadingIntervention(
                    id=created, source_hospital_id=proposal.hospital_id, approved_tick=tick
                )
                kind = "level_loading_approved"
                run.recompute()
            run.approved_proposals.add(proposal.id)
            run.actions.append(
                OperatorAction(kind, tick, now, proposal.hospital_id, proposal.id, operator)
            )
            run.version += 1
            log.info(
                "proposal approved",
                extra={"run_id": run.run_id, "proposal_id": proposal.id, "tick": tick},
            )
            return run, created

    def simulate_reply(
        self, run_id: str, request_id: str, staff_id: str | None = None, reply: str = "IN"
    ) -> tuple[Run, ConfirmationRecord]:
        """Dashboard fallback for a staff reply. Always labeled as simulated."""
        return self._record_reply(run_id, request_id, staff_id, reply, source="simulated")

    def _record_reply(
        self, run_id: str, request_id: str, staff_id: str | None, reply: str, source: str
    ) -> tuple[Run, ConfirmationRecord]:
        with self._lock:
            run = self.get_run(run_id)
            request = run.staffing_requests.get(request_id)
            if request is None:
                raise NotFoundError(f"Staffing request '{request_id}' not found")
            if reply.strip().upper() != "IN":
                raise ConflictError("Only the reply 'IN' confirms a demo shift")
            now = self.clock()
            if now >= request.expires_at:
                raise ConflictError(f"Staffing request '{request_id}' has expired")
            if request.confirmed_staff >= request.requested_staff:
                raise ConflictError(f"Staffing request '{request_id}' is already fully confirmed")
            confirmed_ids = {c.staff_id for c in request.confirmations}
            if staff_id is None:
                staff_id = next((sid for sid, _ in DEMO_STAFF if sid not in confirmed_ids), None)
                if staff_id is None:
                    raise ConflictError("Every fictional demo staff member has already replied")
            elif staff_id not in STAFF_NAMES:
                raise NotFoundError(f"Unknown demo staff member '{staff_id}'")
            elif staff_id in confirmed_ids:
                raise ConflictError(f"'{staff_id}' has already confirmed this request")

            record = ConfirmationRecord(staff_id, STAFF_NAMES[staff_id], source, now, 0.0)
            request.confirmations.append(record)
            record.recompute_ms = run.recompute()
            run.version += 1
            log.info(
                "staff confirmed",
                extra={
                    "run_id": run.run_id,
                    "request_id": request_id,
                    "source": source,
                    "confirmed": request.confirmed_staff,
                    "recompute_ms": record.recompute_ms,
                },
            )
            return run, record

    def request_status(self, request: StaffingRequest) -> str:
        if request.confirmed_staff >= request.requested_staff:
            return "fully_confirmed"
        if self.clock() >= request.expires_at:
            return "expired"
        return "partially_confirmed" if request.confirmed_staff else "awaiting_replies"

"""Builds the single-screen DashboardState (and Diagnostics) from a demo Run."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import asdict
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from app.config import SYNTHETIC_DATA_NOTICE
from app.models.dashboard import (
    Band,
    Confirmation,
    CurvePoint,
    Curves,
    DashboardState,
    Diagnostics,
    Divergence,
    FeedEvent,
    Flow,
    ForecastAccuracy,
    HeroMetric,
    HospitalInfo,
    HospitalPoint,
    HospitalSeries,
    Impact,
    Marker,
    Meta,
    ProposalCard,
    RecoveryView,
    RunInfo,
    ScenarioSummary,
    StaffingRequestView,
    StatusTransition,
    Timeline,
    TimeWindow,
)
from app.services.demo_service import DemoService, Run
from app.simulation.comparison import MetricDelta, track_digest
from app.simulation.forecast import FORECAST_HORIZON_TICKS
from app.simulation.metrics import (
    ambulance_waiting_hours_by_tick,
    hospital_recovery,
)
from app.simulation.models import TICK_MINUTES, EventKind, HospitalTick, RerouteReason, TrackResult

SUGGESTED_MS_PER_TICK = 350  # 24 ticks = about 8.4 seconds of playback

MODEL_LIMITATIONS = (
    "Synthetic model; not clinically validated and not based on real hospital data.",
    "15-minute resolution; one pooled staff number per hospital; no inpatient boarding, "
    "lab or imaging delays, or patients leaving without being seen.",
    "Forecast is a simple fluid projection from the trailing hour; it overshoots during "
    "sudden bursts and can raise false alarms.",
    "Level-loading assumes immediate EMS compliance.",
    "Results are exactly reproducible on one platform and Python version.",
)


def _window(run: Run) -> TimeWindow:
    start, end = run.scenario.demo_window
    c = run.scenario.clock_label
    return TimeWindow(start_tick=start, end_tick=end, start_clock=c(start), end_clock=c(end))


def _point(row: HospitalTick) -> HospitalPoint:
    return HospitalPoint(
        tick=row.tick,
        status=row.status.value,
        saturation_pct=row.saturation_pct,
        occupied=row.occupied,
        queue_length=row.queue_length,
        ambulances_waiting=row.ambulance_queue_length,
        staff_on_duty=row.staff_on_duty,
        staffed_capacity=row.staffed_capacity,
        mean_wait_minutes=row.mean_current_wait_minutes,
        forecast_saturation_pct=row.forecast_saturation_pct,
        diverting=row.diverting,
    )


def _hero(key: str, label: str, unit: str, d: MetricDelta, decimals: int = 1) -> HeroMetric:
    improved = None if d.delta == 0 else d.delta < 0
    magnitude = f"{abs(d.delta):.{decimals}f} {unit}"
    if d.delta == 0:
        headline = "No difference yet"
    else:
        pct = f" ({d.pct_change:+.0f}%)" if d.pct_change is not None else ""
        headline = f"{magnitude} {'less' if improved else 'more'}{pct}"
    return HeroMetric(
        key=key, label=label, unit=unit, baseline=d.baseline, triagex=d.triagex,
        delta=d.delta, pct_change=d.pct_change, lower_is_better=True, improved=improved,
        headline=headline,
    )  # fmt: skip


def _delta(a: float, b: float) -> MetricDelta:
    pct = round((b - a) / a * 100, 1) if a else None
    return MetricDelta(float(a), float(b), round(b - a, 2), pct)


def _active_staffing(run: Run):
    confirmed = [r for r in run.staffing_requests.values() if r.confirmed_staff > 0]
    return min(confirmed, key=lambda r: r.approved_tick, default=None)


def _phase(run: Run, tick: int) -> str:
    request = _active_staffing(run)
    if request is None:
        return "before_intervention"
    iv = request.intervention()
    if tick < iv.approved_tick:
        return "before_intervention"
    if tick < iv.effective_tick:
        return "staff_en_route"
    if tick < iv.end_tick:
        return "shift_active"
    return "after_shift"


def _curves(run: Run, divergence: int | None) -> Curves:
    c = run.comparison
    window = _window(run)
    rng = (window.start_tick, window.end_tick)
    focus = run.scenario.focus_hospital_id
    a_cum = ambulance_waiting_hours_by_tick(c.baseline, rng)
    b_cum = ambulance_waiting_hours_by_tick(c.triagex, rng)
    fa, fb = c.baseline.hospital_series(focus), c.triagex.hospital_series(focus)
    points = []
    for k, t in enumerate(range(*rng)):
        ra, rb = c.baseline.ticks[t], c.triagex.ticks[t]
        points.append(
            CurvePoint(
                tick=t,
                clock=run.scenario.clock_label(t),
                phase=_phase(run, t),
                diverged=divergence is not None and t >= divergence,
                baseline_focus_saturation_pct=fa[t].saturation_pct,
                triagex_focus_saturation_pct=fb[t].saturation_pct,
                baseline_patients_waiting=sum(r.queue_length for r in ra),
                triagex_patients_waiting=sum(r.queue_length for r in rb),
                baseline_ambulances_waiting=sum(r.ambulance_queue_length for r in ra),
                triagex_ambulances_waiting=sum(r.ambulance_queue_length for r in rb),
                baseline_ambulance_hours_cumulative=a_cum[k],
                triagex_ambulance_hours_cumulative=b_cum[k],
                ambulance_hours_saved_so_far=round(a_cum[k] - b_cum[k], 2),
            )
        )
    return Curves(focus_hospital_id=focus, window=window, points=points)


def _recovery(run: Run) -> RecoveryView:
    c, sc = run.comparison, run.scenario
    focus = sc.focus_hospital_id
    rng = (sc.surge_onset_tick, sc.horizon_ticks)
    a, b = hospital_recovery(c.baseline, focus, rng), hospital_recovery(c.triagex, focus, rng)
    name = run.network.get(focus).short_name
    sooner = None
    if a.recovered_tick is not None and b.recovered_tick is not None:
        sooner = (a.recovered_tick - b.recovered_tick) * TICK_MINUTES
    if a.first_breach_tick is None:
        headline = f"{name} stayed below capacity"
    elif sooner is None and b.recovered_tick is not None:
        headline = f"{name} back to normal by {sc.clock_label(b.recovered_tick)}; "
        headline += "without TriageX it had not recovered"
    elif sooner is None:
        headline = f"{name} had not recovered by the end of the simulation"
    elif sooner > 0:
        headline = f"{name} back to normal {sooner} min sooner"
    elif sooner < 0:
        headline = f"{name} back to normal {-sooner} min later"
    else:
        headline = f"{name} recovery time unchanged"
    label = sc.clock_label
    return RecoveryView(
        hospital_id=focus,
        baseline_recovered_tick=a.recovered_tick,
        triagex_recovered_tick=b.recovered_tick,
        baseline_recovered_clock=label(a.recovered_tick) if a.recovered_tick is not None else None,
        triagex_recovered_clock=label(b.recovered_tick) if b.recovered_tick is not None else None,
        minutes_sooner=sooner,
        baseline_breach_hours=a.breach_ticks * TICK_MINUTES / 60,
        triagex_breach_hours=b.breach_ticks * TICK_MINUTES / 60,
        headline=headline,
    )


def _impact(run: Run, curves: Curves) -> Impact:
    c = run.comparison
    last = curves.points[-1]
    primary = _hero(
        "ambulance_handoff_hours",
        "Ambulance hours lost to handoff delays",
        "ambulance hours",
        _delta(last.baseline_ambulance_hours_cumulative, last.triagex_ambulance_hours_cumulative),
    )
    secondary = [
        _hero("mean_wait_minutes", "Average patient wait", "min",
              c.window_deltas["mean_wait_minutes"]),
        _hero("diverted_ambulances", "Ambulances diverted", "ambulances",
              c.window_deltas["diverted_ambulances"], decimals=0),
    ]  # fmt: skip
    has_effect = any(
        r.confirmed_staff > 0 for r in run.staffing_requests.values()
    ) or bool(run.level_loading)
    return Impact(
        state="intervention_scheduled" if has_effect else "awaiting_intervention",
        primary=primary,
        secondary=secondary,
        recovery=_recovery(run),
        window=curves.window,
    )


def _transitions(run: Run) -> list[StatusTransition]:
    out = []
    for track_name, track in (("baseline", run.comparison.baseline),
                              ("triagex", run.comparison.triagex)):  # fmt: skip
        for hid in track.hospital_ids:
            series = track.hospital_series(hid)
            for prev, cur in zip(series, series[1:], strict=False):
                if prev.status is not cur.status:
                    out.append(
                        StatusTransition(
                            tick=cur.tick, clock=run.scenario.clock_label(cur.tick),
                            track=track_name, hospital_id=hid,
                            from_status=prev.status.value, to_status=cur.status.value,
                        )  # fmt: skip
                    )
    return sorted(out, key=lambda x: (x.tick, x.track, x.hospital_id))


def _flows(run: Run) -> list[Flow]:
    groups: dict[tuple, int] = defaultdict(int)
    travel: dict[tuple, int] = {}
    for track_name, track in (("baseline", run.comparison.baseline),
                              ("triagex", run.comparison.triagex)):  # fmt: skip
        for r in track.patients:
            if r.reroute_reason is None or not (0 <= r.original_arrival_tick < track.horizon_ticks):
                continue
            kind = "diversion" if r.reroute_reason is RerouteReason.DIVERSION else "level_loading"
            key = (r.original_arrival_tick, track_name, r.intended_hospital_id,
                   r.final_hospital_id, kind)  # fmt: skip
            groups[key] += 1
            travel[key] = r.extra_travel_ticks
    return [
        Flow(tick=k[0], track=k[1], from_hospital_id=k[2], to_hospital_id=k[3], kind=k[4],
             count=n, travel_ticks=travel[k])  # fmt: skip
        for k, n in sorted(groups.items())
    ]


def _proposal_title(run: Run, kind: str, hospital_id: str, staff: int | None) -> str:
    name = run.network.get(hospital_id).short_name
    if kind == "staffing":
        return f"Call in {staff} staff at {name}"
    return f"Level-load ambulances away from {name}"


def _cards(run: Run, only_window: bool) -> list[ProposalCard]:
    recommended = run.recommended_proposal()
    start, end = run.scenario.demo_window
    seen: dict[str, ProposalCard] = {}
    for p in [*run.comparison.triagex.proposals, *run.baseline.proposals]:
        if p.id in seen:
            continue
        approved = p.id in run.approved_proposals
        if only_window and not approved and not (start <= p.tick < end):
            continue
        if p.id not in {q.id for q in run.comparison.triagex.proposals} and not approved:
            continue  # no longer raised in the operator's (TriageX) future
        seen[p.id] = ProposalCard(
            id=p.id, kind=p.kind, hospital_id=p.hospital_id, tick=p.tick,
            clock=run.scenario.clock_label(p.tick),
            title=_proposal_title(run, p.kind, p.hospital_id, p.recommended_staff),
            rationale=p.rationale, forecast_saturation_pct=p.forecast_saturation_pct,
            current_saturation_pct=p.current_saturation_pct,
            recommended_staff=p.recommended_staff,
            status="approved" if approved else "available",
            recommended=recommended is not None and p.id == recommended.id,
        )  # fmt: skip
    return sorted(seen.values(), key=lambda x: (x.tick, x.hospital_id, x.kind))


def _requests(service: DemoService, run: Run) -> list[StaffingRequestView]:
    out = []
    for r in run.staffing_requests.values():
        effect = next(
            (e for e in run.comparison.intervention_effects if e.intervention_id == r.request_id),
            None,
        )
        iv = r.intervention()
        out.append(
            StaffingRequestView(
                request_id=r.request_id, proposal_id=r.proposal_id, hospital_id=r.hospital_id,
                requested_staff=r.requested_staff, confirmed_staff=r.confirmed_staff,
                usable_staff=effect.usable_staff if effect and effect.usable_staff else 0,
                status=service.request_status(r), approved_tick=r.approved_tick,
                effective_tick=iv.effective_tick, end_tick=iv.end_tick,
                approved_at=r.approved_at, expires_at=r.expires_at,
                confirmations=[
                    Confirmation(staff_id=c.staff_id, display_name=c.display_name,
                                 source=c.source, received_at=c.received_at)
                    for c in r.confirmations
                ],
            )  # fmt: skip
        )
    return out


def _feed(run: Run, divergence: int | None) -> list[FeedEvent]:
    sc, c, net = run.scenario, run.comparison, run.network
    label = sc.clock_label
    events: list[tuple[int, int, FeedEvent]] = []

    def add(rank: int, **kw) -> None:
        tick = kw["tick"]
        kw.setdefault("clock", label(tick))
        kw.setdefault("id", f"{kw['kind']}:{tick}:{kw.get('hospital_id') or ''}:{len(events)}")
        events.append((tick, rank, FeedEvent(**kw)))

    add(0, tick=sc.surge_onset_tick, title="Surge Begins", detail=sc.name, kind="surge_onset",
        track="both", origin="simulation", severity="warning")
    for p in c.triagex.proposals:
        if p.kind != "staffing":
            continue
        name = net.get(p.hospital_id).short_name
        add(1, tick=p.tick, title="Surge Predicted",
            detail=f"{name}: 2-hour forecast {p.forecast_saturation_pct:.0f}% of treatment spaces",
            kind="surge_predicted", track="triagex", origin="simulation",
            severity="critical" if p.forecast_saturation_pct >= 100 else "warning",
            hospital_id=p.hospital_id)  # fmt: skip
    for a in run.actions:
        name = net.get(a.hospital_id).short_name
        if a.kind == "outreach_approved":
            title, detail = "Outreach Approved", f"Staff outreach approved for {name}"
        else:
            title, detail = "Level-Loading Approved", f"Redirect low-acuity ambulances from {name}"
        add(2, tick=a.tick, title=title, detail=detail, kind=a.kind, track="triagex",
            origin="operator", severity="info", hospital_id=a.hospital_id, wall_time=a.wall_time)
    for r in run.staffing_requests.values():
        name = net.get(r.hospital_id).short_name
        for i, conf in enumerate(r.confirmations, start=1):
            add(3, tick=r.approved_tick, title="Staff Confirmed",
                detail=f"{conf.display_name} confirmed for {name} ({i}/{r.requested_staff})",
                kind="staff_confirmed", track="triagex", origin=conf.source,
                severity="success", hospital_id=r.hospital_id, wall_time=conf.received_at)
            add(4, tick=r.approved_tick, title="Capacity Recalculated",
                detail=f"With TriageX future recalculated in {conf.recompute_ms:.0f} ms",
                kind="recalculated", track="triagex", origin="simulation", severity="info",
                hospital_id=r.hospital_id, wall_time=conf.received_at)  # fmt: skip
    for track_name, track in (("baseline", c.baseline), ("triagex", c.triagex)):
        side = "Without TriageX" if track_name == "baseline" else "With TriageX"
        for e in track.events:
            name = net.get(e.hospital_id).short_name
            if e.kind is EventKind.DIVERSION_START:
                add(5, tick=e.tick, title="Diversion Started", detail=f"{side}: {name} diverts ambulances",
                    kind="diversion_start", track=track_name, origin="simulation",
                    severity="critical", hospital_id=e.hospital_id)  # fmt: skip
            elif e.kind is EventKind.DIVERSION_END:
                add(5, tick=e.tick, title="Diversion Ended", detail=f"{side}: {name} reopens",
                    kind="diversion_end", track=track_name, origin="simulation",
                    severity="info", hospital_id=e.hospital_id)  # fmt: skip
            elif track_name == "triagex" and e.kind is EventKind.STAFF_SHIFT_ACTIVE:
                add(6, tick=e.tick, title="Shift Active",
                    detail=f"{e.detail['added_staff']} confirmed staff on the floor at {name}",
                    kind="shift_active", track="triagex", origin="simulation",
                    severity="success", hospital_id=e.hospital_id)  # fmt: skip
            elif track_name == "triagex" and e.kind is EventKind.STAFF_SHIFT_ENDED:
                add(6, tick=e.tick, title="Shift Ended", detail=f"Surge shift at {name} ends",
                    kind="shift_end", track="triagex", origin="simulation", severity="info",
                    hospital_id=e.hospital_id)  # fmt: skip
            elif track_name == "triagex" and e.kind is EventKind.LEVEL_LOADING_ACTIVE:
                add(6, tick=e.tick, title="Level-Loading Active",
                    detail=f"Low-acuity ambulances redirected from {name}",
                    kind="level_loading_active", track="triagex", origin="simulation",
                    severity="success", hospital_id=e.hospital_id)  # fmt: skip
    if divergence is not None:
        add(7, tick=divergence, title="Futures Diverge",
            detail="The two simulated futures separate from here", kind="divergence",
            track="both", origin="simulation", severity="success")  # fmt: skip
    rec = _recovery(run)
    for track_name, tick in (("baseline", rec.baseline_recovered_tick),
                             ("triagex", rec.triagex_recovered_tick)):  # fmt: skip
        if tick is not None:
            side = "Without TriageX" if track_name == "baseline" else "With TriageX"
            name = net.get(rec.hospital_id).short_name
            add(8, tick=tick, title="Back to Normal", detail=f"{side}: {name} below 85%",
                kind="recovered", track=track_name, origin="simulation", severity="success",
                hospital_id=rec.hospital_id)  # fmt: skip
    events.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))
    return [e for _, _, e in events]


def _bands(run: Run) -> list[Band]:
    start, end = run.scenario.demo_window
    bands = [Band(kind="demo_window", start_tick=start, end_tick=end, label="6-hour demo window")]
    for r in run.staffing_requests.values():
        iv = r.intervention()
        bands.append(Band(kind="staff_lead_time", start_tick=iv.approved_tick,
                          end_tick=iv.effective_tick, label="Staff en route (45 min)",
                          hospital_id=r.hospital_id))  # fmt: skip
        if r.confirmed_staff:
            bands.append(Band(kind="shift_active", start_tick=iv.effective_tick,
                              end_tick=iv.end_tick, label="Surge shift active",
                              hospital_id=r.hospital_id))  # fmt: skip
    for iv in run.level_loading.values():
        bands.append(Band(kind="level_loading_active", start_tick=iv.effective_tick,
                          end_tick=iv.end_tick, label="Level-loading active",
                          hospital_id=iv.hospital_id))  # fmt: skip
    return bands


MARKER_LABELS = {
    "surge_onset": "Surge Begins",
    "proposal": "Surge Predicted",
    "approval": "Outreach Approved",
    "shift_active": "Shift Active",
    "shift_end": "Shift Ended",
    "level_loading_active": "Level-Loading Active",
    "level_loading_end": "Level-Loading Ended",
    "divergence": "Futures Diverge",
    "baseline_diversion": "Diversion (without TriageX)",
}


def _markers(run: Run) -> list[Marker]:
    out = []
    for m in run.comparison.markers:
        if m.kind in ("demo_window_start", "demo_window_end"):
            continue
        if m.kind == "proposal" and "staffing" not in (m.intervention_id or ""):
            continue
        if m.kind == "approval" and m.intervention_id in run.level_loading:
            label = "Level-Loading Approved"
        else:
            label = MARKER_LABELS.get(m.kind, m.label)
        out.append(Marker(tick=m.tick, clock=m.clock, kind=m.kind, label=label,
                          hospital_id=m.hospital_id))  # fmt: skip
    return out


def build_dashboard(service: DemoService, run: Run) -> DashboardState:
    started = time.perf_counter()
    sc, c = run.scenario, run.comparison
    divergence = c.first_divergence_tick
    curves = _curves(run, divergence)
    state = DashboardState(
        run=RunInfo(
            run_id=run.run_id, version=run.version, seed=run.seed, created_at=run.created_at,
            notice=SYNTHETIC_DATA_NOTICE,
            scenario=ScenarioSummary(id=sc.id, name=sc.name, description=sc.description,
                                     focus_hospital_id=sc.focus_hospital_id,
                                     surge_onset_tick=sc.surge_onset_tick),
        ),  # fmt: skip
        timeline=Timeline(
            tick_minutes=TICK_MINUTES, horizon_ticks=sc.horizon_ticks,
            clocks=[sc.clock_label(t) for t in range(sc.horizon_ticks)],
            demo_window=_window(run), suggested_ms_per_tick=SUGGESTED_MS_PER_TICK,
        ),  # fmt: skip
        hospitals=[
            HospitalInfo(id=h.id, name=h.name, short_name=h.short_name, lat=h.lat, lon=h.lon,
                         treatment_spaces=h.treatment_spaces, base_staff=h.base_staff)
            for h in run.network.hospitals
        ],  # fmt: skip
        series=[
            HospitalSeries(
                hospital_id=hid,
                baseline=[_point(r) for r in c.baseline.hospital_series(hid)],
                triagex=[_point(r) for r in c.triagex.hospital_series(hid)],
            )
            for hid in c.baseline.hospital_ids
        ],
        curves=curves,
        bands=_bands(run),
        markers=_markers(run),
        transitions=_transitions(run),
        flows=_flows(run),
        feed=_feed(run, divergence),
        proposals=_cards(run, only_window=True),
        staffing_requests=_requests(service, run),
        impact=_impact(run, curves),
        divergence=Divergence(tick=divergence, clock=sc.clock_label(divergence))
        if divergence is not None
        else None,
        meta=Meta(generated_at=datetime.now(UTC), recompute_ms=run.last_recompute_ms, build_ms=0),
    )
    state.meta.build_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
    return state


def _forecast_accuracy(track: TrackResult) -> ForecastAccuracy:
    errors = []
    for hid in track.hospital_ids:
        s = track.hospital_series(hid)
        for t in range(len(s) - FORECAST_HORIZON_TICKS):
            errors.append(s[t].forecast_saturation_pct - s[t + FORECAST_HORIZON_TICKS].saturation_pct)
    n = len(errors) or 1
    return ForecastAccuracy(
        REDACTED * TICK_MINUTES,
        samples=len(errors),
        bias_pct_points=round(sum(errors) / n, 2),
        mean_absolute_error_pct_points=round(sum(abs(e) for e in errors) / n, 2),
    )


def build_diagnostics(run: Run) -> Diagnostics:
    c = run.comparison

    def jsonable(obj):
        return {k: (v.value if hasattr(v, "value") else v) for k, v in asdict(obj).items()}

    return Diagnostics(
        run_id=run.run_id,
        version=run.version,
        scenario_assumptions=list(run.scenario.assumptions),
        model_limitations=list(MODEL_LIMITATIONS),
        forecast_accuracy=_forecast_accuracy(run.baseline),
        all_proposals=_cards(run, only_window=False),
        intervention_effects=[asdict(e) for e in c.intervention_effects],
        full_horizon_metrics={"baseline": jsonable(c.baseline_metrics),
                              "triagex": jsonable(c.triagex_metrics)},
        demo_window_metrics={"baseline": jsonable(c.window_baseline_metrics),
                             "triagex": jsonable(c.window_triagex_metrics)},
        track_digests={"baseline": track_digest(c.baseline), "triagex": track_digest(c.triagex)},
        recompute_history_ms=list(run.recompute_history_ms),
    )  # fmt: skip

"""TriageX backend entrypoint."""

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.middleware.gzip import GZipMiddleware

from app.api.health import router as health_router
from app.api.reference import router as reference_router
from app.api.runs import router as runs_router
from app.api.ws import ConnectionManager
from app.api.ws import router as ws_router
from app.config import APP_NAME, get_settings
from app.logging_config import configure_logging
from app.services.demo_service import DemoService


def create_app(demo_service: DemoService | None = None) -> FastAPI:
    settings = get_settings()
    configure_logging(settings.log_level)

    app = FastAPI(title=f"{APP_NAME} API", version="0.3.0")
    app.state.demo_service = demo_service or DemoService()
    app.state.ws_manager = ConnectionManager()
    app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, minimum_size=2048)
    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=settings.cors_origin_list,
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )
    app.include_router(health_router, prefix="/api")
    app.include_router(reference_router, prefix="/api")
    app.include_router(runs_router, prefix="/api")
    app.include_router(ws_router)
    return app


app = create_app()

"""Phase 3 API: single-screen dashboard state, demo flow, reset, errors, and latency."""

import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import create_app
from app.services.demo_service import DemoService
from app.simulation.comparison import run_comparison
from app.simulation.interventions import StaffingIntervention
from app.simulation.metrics import ambulance_waiting_hours_by_tick
from app.simulation.scenarios import SCENARIOS


class FakeClock:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.now = datetime(2026, 11, 14, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)

    def __call__(self) -> datetime:
        return self.now


@pytest.fixture
def clock():
    return FakeClock()


@pytest.fixture
def client(clock):
    service = DemoService(request_ttl=timedelta(minutes=10), clock=clock)
    with TestClient(create_app(service)) as c:
        yield c


def _reset(client, **body):
    r = client.post("/api/demo/reset", json=body or None)
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.json()


def _approve_recommended(client, state):
    pid = next(p["id"] for p in state["proposals"] if p["recommended"])
    r = client.post(f"/api/runs/{state['run']['run_id']}/proposals/{pid}/approve")
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.json()


def _reply(client, state, **body):
    run_id = state["run"]["run_id"]
    request_id = state["staffing_requests"][0]["request_id"]
    return client.post(
        f"/api/runs/{run_id}/staffing-requests/{request_id}/simulate-reply", json=body or None
    )


def _confirm_all(client):
    state = _approve_recommended(client, _reset(client))
    for _ in range(state["staffing_requests"][0]["requested_staff"]):
        r = _reply(client, state)
        assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
        state = r.json()
    return state


# --- initial state --------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_reset_returns_ready_to_render_i85_state(client):
    s = _reset(client)
    assert s["run"]["scenario"]["id"] == "i85_pileup"
    assert s["run"]["seed"] == 42
    assert "not real-time hospital data" in s["run"]["notice"]
    assert len(s["timeline"]["clocks"]) == 96
    window = s["timeline"]["demo_window"]

# TriageX API (Phase 3)

This is the backend contract for the single-screen command center. Every number in a
response is computed by the deterministic simulation; the frontend never calculates
deltas or percentages itself.

- Base URL in development: `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Use `127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`. On
  Windows, `localhost` tries IPv6 first and adds about 200 ms to every request.
- The Vite dev server proxies `/api` and `/ws` to the backend.
- Interactive schema: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (OpenAPI).

## Demo flow in four calls

| Step | Call | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Reset | `POST /api/demo/reset` | Fresh I-85 run, seed 42. Both futures are identical. |
| 2. Approve outreach | `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/proposals/{proposal_id}/approve` | Creates a staffing request. No outcome changes yet. |
| 3. Staff confirms (repeat) | `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/staffing-requests/{request_id}/simulate-reply` | Adds one confirmation and recalculates Track B. |
| 4. Read diagnostics (optional) | `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/diagnostics` | Engineering detail for judge Q&A. |

Every `POST` returns the complete `DashboardState`, so the screen re-renders from the
response without another request.

For step 2, use the card with `recommended: true` in `proposals`.

In step 3, each confirmation counts in the simulation from the approved request tick
plus 45 simulated minutes. That holds no matter when the reply arrives in real time.
History is never rewritten: ticks before that point are identical in both tracks.

Measured on the development laptop (live uvicorn, curl, 5 rounds × 3 replies):

| Operation | Time |
|---|---|
| One confirmation, end to end | 25–30 ms (about 12 ms recalculating Track B, about 4 ms building the payload) |
| Reset | about 47 ms |

The payload is about 245 KB uncompressed and about 12 KB with gzip.

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | Liveness, branding, synthetic-data notice |
| `GET /api/integrations/health` | Simulation `ok`; database, AI and Chert report `not_implemented` until their phases |
| `GET /api/hospitals` | Map pins (synthetic capacity) |
| `GET /api/scenarios` | Scenario selector |
| `POST /api/demo/reset` | Body (optional): `{scenario_id, seed}`. Discards all runs and returns a new, identical initial state |
| `GET /api/demo/state` | The active run's state (for a second screen or a page refresh) |
| `POST /api/runs` | Body: `{scenario_id, seed}`. New run without discarding others |
| `GET /api/runs/{run_id}` | Current `DashboardState` |
| `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/proposals/{proposal_id}/approve` | Body (optional): `{at_tick, operator}`. `at_tick` defaults to the proposal tick |
| `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/staffing-requests/{request_id}/simulate-reply` | Body (optional): `{staff_id, reply: "IN"}`. Recorded as `simulated` |
| `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/diagnostics` | Assumptions, limitations, forecast accuracy, all proposals, digests, recompute timings |

Error codes:

- **404:** unknown run, proposal, request or staff member.
- **409:** a state conflict. That covers approving a proposal twice, approving before
  the proposal tick, a reply other than `IN`, a duplicate reply, a fully confirmed
  request, or an expired request (10 minutes of real time).
- **422:** invalid input.

## WebSocket `/ws`

Every message is JSON, sent from the server to the client:

```json
{"type": "hello", "run_id": "…", "version": 3}
{"type": "run.updated", "run_id": "…", "version": 4, "reason": "staff_confirmed", "recompute_ms": 12.4}
```

- `reason` is one of `reset`, `run_created`, `proposal_approved` or `staff_confirmed`.
- A screen that did not make the change refetches `GET /api/runs/{run_id}` when the
  version increases.
- The client may send `{"type": "ping"}` and receives `{"type": "pong"}`.

## `DashboardState` at a glance

| Field | Renders | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `run` | Header | Includes `notice`, the synthetic-data label that must stay on screen |
| `timeline` | Slider | `clocks[tick]` labels, `demo_window` (24 ticks, 15:00–21:00 for I-85), `suggested_ms_per_tick` |
| `hospitals` + `series` | Map | Per hospital, 96 points per track: status, saturation, queue, ambulances waiting, staff, forecast, diverting |
| `curves` | Comparison charts | Demo window only, both futures side by side; see below |
| `bands` | Shaded chart regions | `demo_window`, `staff_lead_time` (approval to shift start), `shift_active`, `level_loading_active` |
| `markers` | Vertical chart lines | "Surge Begins", "Surge Predicted", "Outreach Approved", "Shift Active", "Futures Diverge"… |
| `transitions` | Map color changes | Status changes per track and hospital |
| `flows` | Map arcs | Rerouted ambulances per tick: `diversion` or `level_loading` |
| `feed` | Coordination feed | Concise titles; `track`, `origin` and `severity` included |
| `proposals` | Action cards | Demo-window cards plus the recommended one |
| `staffing_requests` | Outreach panel | Requested, confirmed and usable staff, status, confirmations with `source` |
| `impact` | Hero metric | `primary` = ambulance hours lost to handoff delays; `secondary` = average wait and diverted ambulances; `recovery` |
| `divergence` | "Futures Diverge" moment | `null` until an intervention changes the future |
| `meta` | Dev overlay | `recompute_ms`, `build_ms` |

### `curves.points[]` (one per demo-window tick)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `phase` | `before_intervention`, `staff_en_route`, `shift_active` or `after_shift`. Use it to style the curve. |
| `diverged` | `false` for every tick before the first difference. Both lines draw on top of each other until then. |
| `baseline_*` / `triagex_*` | Focus-hospital saturation, network patients waiting, network ambulances waiting, cumulative ambulance-hours |
| `ambulance_hours_saved_so_far` | The running hero counter. It is 0 until the futures diverge and equals `impact.primary` at the window's end. |

**Honest playback rule:** while the playhead is at tick `t`, show
`curves.points[t].ambulance_hours_saved_so_far` as the live counter. Show the final
`impact` figures only when playback reaches the end of the window. The counter can then
never show an improvement before the intervention is active.

### Hero metric definitions

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Ambulance hours lost to handoff delays** (primary) | Sum over demo-window ticks of ambulances waiting for a treatment space at the end of each tick × 15 min. Network-wide, derived from tick state. |
| **Average patient wait** | Mean wait from ED arrival to treatment space for patients arriving in the window. Patients still waiting at the end of the horizon count with their wait so far. |
| **Ambulances diverted** | Ambulances rerouted by diversion, for arrivals in the window |
| **Recovery** | First tick after the focus hospital's first breach that starts a full simulated hour below 85% saturation |

Each `HeroMetric` carries `baseline`, `triagex`, `delta` (TriageX minus baseline),
`pct_change`, `improved` (`null` when equal) and a ready-made `headline`, for example
"11.5 fewer ambulance hours lost (−45%)".

## Current I-85 result (seed 42)

The run approves the recommended Grady staffing proposal at 16:15. Track B changes only
after the confirmed staff start their shift at 17:00.

| Confirmed staff | Primary headline | Average wait | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.5 fewer ambulance hours lost (−26%) | 4.2 min shorter (−29%) | 15 min sooner |
| 2 | 9.8 fewer ambulance hours lost (−38%) | 6.2 min shorter (−44%) | 45 min sooner |
| 3 | 11.5 fewer ambulance hours lost (−45%) | 7.4 min shorter (−52%) | 45 min sooner |

These are model outputs, not targets. Other scenarios and seeds give different results;
see [assumptions.md](assumptions.md).

Phase 3 is built. A staff confirmation now updates the comparison in 25–30 ms end to end, measured against a live server, well under your 200 ms target. Nothing is committed or pushed yet, because you haven't asked for that this phase. Say the word and I'll commit it as a separate checkpoint, push it and check Entire's sync, as in Phase 2.

I took this message as approval to start Phase 3. No frontend, database, Chert or AI work is included.

## How the API supports the 90-second demo

The demo runs in four calls, and every `POST` returns the whole single-screen state, so the screen never waits on a second request:

1. **Reset** (`POST /api/demo/reset`): starts the I-85 scenario on seed 42. Both futures are identical.
2. **Approve** the one proposal marked `recommended`, "Call in 3 staff at Grady" at 16:15. Nothing changes yet.
3. **Simulate a staff reply**, up to three times. Each reply re-simulates only the TriageX track (about 12 ms).
4. **Diagnostics** (optional, a separate endpoint): assumptions, limitations, forecast accuracy and all proposals, kept off the presentation screen for judge Q&A.

Result for I-85, seed 42, as the replies come in:

| Confirmed staff | Headline returned by the API |
|---|---|
| 1 | 6.5 fewer ambulance hours lost (−26%); Grady back to normal 15 min sooner |
| 2 | 9.8 fewer ambulance hours lost (−38%); 45 min sooner |
| 3 | 11.5 fewer ambulance hours lost (−45%); 7.4 min shorter average wait (−52%); 3 fewer ambulances diverted (−30%); 45 min sooner |

The other three scenarios also produce a recommended proposal inside their demo window, with improvements of 22–42% in ambulance hours.

## Keeping the story honest on screen

- **Curves:** the six-hour window carries a `phase` and a `diverged` flag on every tick. The two lines are identical until the shift starts at 17:00, and the API marks the "Futures Diverge" moment.
- **Lead-time bands:** "Staff en route (45 min)" and "Surge shift active" come back as chart bands.
- **Live counter:** each tick also carries `ambulance_hours_saved_so_far`. It stays at 0 until the futures diverge, so the screen can't show an improvement before the intervention is active.
- **Feed:** events use your titles: Surge Predicted, Outreach Approved, Staff Confirmed, Capacity Recalculated, Shift Active, Futures Diverge, Back to Normal. Events that are identical in both futures, such as "Grady diverts ambulances" at 16:45, appear once.
- **Simulated replies** are labeled `simulated_reply`.
- **Synthetic-data notice:** it stays in the main payload, as your original spec requires.
- **Integration status:** database, AI and Chert report `not_implemented`, never `ok`.

## Latency

| Path | Time |
|---|---|
| Confirmation, direct to the server | 25–30 ms |
| Confirmation, through the Vite dev proxy | 27–28 ms |
| Reset | about 47 ms |

The payload is about 245 KB, or about 12 KB with gzip.

My first measurement was about 225 ms. That was Windows resolving `localhost` through IPv6 before falling back, not the API. I changed the Vite proxy and dev script to use `127.0.0.1`. That is the only frontend file I touched, a one-line config change.

## Tests

- **Backend:** 105 pass, 19 of them new.
- **Lint:** Ruff is clean.
- **Frontend:** the existing 2 tests pass and the build succeeds.

The new tests cover:
- reset returning an identical state every time;
- approval alone changing nothing;
- the baseline track never changing after confirmations;
- hero numbers matching the engine computed independently;
- the under-200 ms round trip;
- 404, 409 and 422 errors, including request expiry with a fake clock;
- the WebSocket push.

## Files

New:
- **Backend:** `app/api/runs.py`, `app/api/reference.py`, `app/api/ws.py`, `app/models/dashboard.py`, `app/services/demo_service.py`, `app/services/dashboard.py`
- **Tests:** `tests/test_api_demo.py`
- **Docs:** [docs/api.md](docs/api.md), the contract the frontend phase will build against

Modified:
- **Backend:** `app/main.py`, `app/api/health.py`, plus small additions in the simulation (focus hospital per scenario, two new metrics, an incremental comparison builder)
- **Dev setup:** `frontend/vite.config.ts`, `scripts/dev.ps1`
- **Docs:** `README.md`, `docs/plan.md`

## Open points

- Runs live in memory and are lost when the server restarts; Phase 4 adds Tiger Data.
- The AI brief endpoint is deferred to Phase 5.

Phase 3 complete. Awaiting approval to begin Phase 4.

content.text:
The proposal time was being used as the approval time. I fixed it, committed it as `ed27758` ("feat: add TriageX live simulation API"), pushed it, and Entire's checkpoint is synced.

**What went wrong:** the engine always ran the 45 minutes from whatever approval tick it was given, so both phases were internally correct. The difference was the tick each caller passed in:
- **Phase 2 command-line tool:** approved one tick (15 minutes) after the proposal: 16:15 → 16:30 → 17:15.
- **Phase 3 API:** when the client didn't send an approval tick, it silently used the proposal tick. That gave 16:15 → 16:15 → 17:00, which assumed an instant approval nobody made.

**What changed:**
- The approve call now requires `at_tick`, the simulated time the operator actually clicked (the playhead position). It is rejected with a 422 error if missing, and with a 409 if it is earlier than the proposal.
- Each staffing request now reports its proposal, approval and activation times separately.
- The "Outreach Approved" feed event says when staff will be on the floor.

**Confirmed I-85 timeline:**

| Event | Simulated time |
|---|---|
| Surge Predicted | 16:15 |
| Outreach Approved | 16:30 |
| Staff Confirmed (inside the 45-minute "Staff en route" band) | 16:30 |
| Shift Active (Grady staff 13 → 16) and Futures Diverge | 17:15 |

A test checks that the request, chart bands, feed, markers, curve phases and staffing levels all agree on this timeline. Another checks that approving 4 ticks later moves activation exactly 4 ticks later.

**Your other checks:**
- **Baseline unchanged:** the baseline track's fingerprint is identical before approval and after each of three confirmations. The TriageX track's fingerprint changes with every confirmation.
- **Impact numbers match the response:** a test recomputes the hero ambulance-hours from the hospital series in the same response and gets exactly the same values. The curve points also match that series tick by tick.
- **Simulated replies are never shown as real Chert messages:** they are labeled `simulated` in the request and `simulated_reply` in the feed, and the feed text reads "via simulated reply". A test checks that nothing in the feed claims a webhook, a sent message, or Chert.
- **25–30 ms is the real API round trip:** it is curl's full HTTP time against the running server, across 15 confirmations: 25.7–28.2 ms. Of that, about 12 ms is recalculating the TriageX track and 4–6 ms is building the response; serialization and transport make up the rest.

**I-85 results with the corrected 16:30 approval:**

| Confirmed staff | Ambulance hours lost | Average wait | Ambulances diverted | Grady recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.5 fewer (−22%) | 3.8 min shorter (−27%) | No change | 30 min sooner |
| 2 | 8.2 fewer (−32%) | 5.8 min shorter (−41%) | 3 fewer (−30%) | 45 min sooner |
| 3 | 9.2 fewer (−36%) | 6.8 min shorter (−48%) | 3 fewer (−30%) | 45 min sooner |

These are smaller than the earlier 11.5 hours because the shift now starts 15 minutes later. I also changed the wording so a metric that hasn't moved reads "No change" once an intervention exists, instead of "No difference yet". docs/api.md has the corrected timeline, required request body and figures.

**Final checks:**
- Backend: 109 tests passed. Ruff lint and format are clean.
- Frontend: 2 tests passed. Build and lint are clean.

**Git and Entire:**
- **Commit:** `ed277585b911a56f4672dd2035c53dbf15fec5b9`, pushed; local `main` matches GitHub.
- **Checkpoint:** `01M7C649ZAB0Y29D6XANM09R12` is on GitHub, and nothing is waiting to sync.
- **History:** your earlier `0d3f825` ("dashboards") had already committed and pushed the original Phase 3 code, so Phase 3 is two commits. I didn't squash them, because that would mean force-pushing over history already on GitHub. Its checkpoint `01M7C5XXZNAG0QADMKRA0SS14P` is synced as well.

Phase 3 complete. Awaiting approval to begin Phase 4.
